title: Becoming an Assistant Professor
abstract: In this session, I will discuss my journey in obtaining a tenure-track position. I will share my experiences as a postdoc, the impact of COVID, the application process, and the benefits of participating in AIChE-sponsored programs such as the Meet the Faculty Candidates Poster Session, Future Faculty Mentoring Program, and Summer School for Engineering Faculty. I will discuss the transition in responsibilities and expectations from postdoc to a new assistant professor as well as the transition from degrees in chemical engineering to research in biomedical engineering.
presenting_author: Sophia Orbach | University of Michigan, Ann Arbor
authors: Sophia Orbach | University of Michigan, Ann Arbor

title: Transition in Progress
abstract: In this session, I will share my path to becoming tenure-track faculty and the multiple transitions along the way that have included being an industrial intern, an instructor, an administrator, and subsequently changing institutions prior to obtaining tenure. This conversation will offer an opportunity to the unique path that also included finding/working with appropriate mentors, a supportive environment, and empowering your young researchers to do the same.
presenting_author: Damilola Daramola | Northeastern University, Boston, MA
authors: Damilola Daramola | Northeastern University, Boston, MA

topic: Learning on the Job: Launching an Academic Career
title: Learning on the Job: Launching an Academic Career
abstract: I will share strategies for successfully pursuing, evolving, and refining the vision that brought you to academia. This will intersect with topics regarding group management, including how to empower group members to feel ownership over the way in which the group is run and how to experiment not just in your science but in the operation of a group. Many of the changes that happen upon starting a junior faculty career involve learning on the job – doing things that you were not trained to do, and we will discuss strategies for adapting to a new set of circumstances. Mechanisms for evolving in the role will be presented as well. Overall, the strategies outlined here will provide a path to not just advancing your scientific vision but staying true to the values you hold inside and outside academia.
presenting_author: Karthish Manthiram | California Institute of Technology, Pasadena
authors: Karthish Manthiram | California Institute of Technology, Pasadena

topic: Making Your Research Matter: Strategies for Successful Broader Impacts Statements
title: Making Your Research Matter: Strategies for Successful Broader Impacts Statements
abstract: This oral presentation is aimed at new faculty starting their careers and focuses on best practices for writing a strong Broader Impacts Statement for NSF proposals. The presentation emphasizes the importance of considering the impact of scientific research on society beyond the lab and highlights the role of the Broader Impacts Statement as a crucial aspect of any research proposal submitted to NSF. The presentation identifies various strategies for creating a successful Broader Impacts Statement, including identifying desired societal outcomes, selecting relevant evidence-based practices for dissemination, finding collaborators, and incorporating the Broader Impacts Impact Framework. Additionally, the presentation emphasizes the importance of evaluating the impact of proposed educational activities, and accounting for the time and costs associated with broader impacts activities. It also covers common pitfalls to avoid in writing a Broader Impacts Statement, such as a generic or unrealistic educational component, reinventing the wheel with an outreach deliverable, and focusing solely on education. The presentation is intended to provide new faculty with practical guidance for writing a strong Broader Impacts Statement that advances science and society while increasing the fundability of NSF proposals.
